On a whim, I purchased a lot of wheat pennies. I remember my dad used to collect them and always found them cool. I've gone through and checked them all and I don't seem to have any particularly valuable pennies but I wanted to see how you guys thought I did on the buy:

US $24.95 + US $4.99 shipping

After sorting them all, I ended up with 508 pennies between 1910 and 1950, I got every year except: 1914, 1915, 1924, and 1931. The builk of the pennies are of course in the 1940s and 50s and I luckily did get some extremely good condition pennies (They don't look like they were cleaned/attempted to have the tarnish removed but they do appear to be uncirculated.)

I should note I'm not a coin collector... yet? But, I wondered what you guys and girls thought about the purchase? Did I do well? Is there any advice you have on any future purchases of lots? What would you estimate the value of my small collection to be? (Roughly) Also, I plan on just keeping them in the family to pass on to grand kids some day cause I always thought handling old money was neat as a kid, are there any precautions I should take in storing them?
Hey /v/coins, I just joined and I'd like some sage wisdom

I won't be able to offer you any sage wisdom since I only mildly dabble in coins myself, but I would say you did good. It'd be hard to guess a value but I'd say you could probably safely assume that you got more than you paid.

There's a table of wheat penny values on this page if you want to get a more specific idea

http://coins.about.com/library/US-coin-values/bl-US0001-Lincoln-Wheat-Values.htm

Purchasing lots pretty much relies on luck, but it is a good way to start learning about coins and what to look for

I went through coin values when I sorted them and put them in a spreadsheet using mostly the assumed low value on each coin and came up with a 'value' of around 200 bucks, I don't feel like that is accurate though.

Just going off of the info you gave I'd probably put the value a little lower (and again I'm not an expert). Wheat coins are pretty common so you should generally assume that you'd get a little less. If you added em up and they came out to around 200, I'd probably say figure a value of somewhere around 100

To hell if you over spent (not saying that you did.), if you enjoyed it then you did good. Sounds like it was a random grab box that had already been searched. But if you got enjoyment out of your investment and it leads you to a new hobby, then you did great.
Aye, I went in assuming it had been searched previously, I was pretty happy to find most years.
Yeah that's really cool. You have most of the run minus some key dates. I personally spent about 6 bucks on a roll of wheaties. So your deal is a lot better.

The Kingkiller Chronicles - Patrick Rothfuss (very good story telling, last chapter still being written, waiting impatiently)

The Warded Man - Peter V. Brett (very unique fantasy world)
